name: The Empress

description2: They are the impulse that draws things together and generates new forms — the same power that animates art, relationships, ecosystems, and imagination. It is the passionate engagement with existence itself.

name: The Emperor

description2: Action is necessary for actualization.

This card invites reflection on what is sacred to you, what knowledge is worth cultivating, and how insight can be shared responsibly. They embody the principle that understanding and action are strongest when informed by careful study, ethical consideration, and the lineage of those who have gone before.

description2: Connection is fertile. Interaction generates insight, reflection, and growth.

description1: Courage and perseverance flourish when paired with self-compassion and the recognition that we are not separate from the natural and instinctive parts of ourselves - our animal nature, our intense emotions, our wilderness.

description2: Insight often comes in the quiet moments.

description2: More a sphere than a wheel: any point can be on top, movement can occur in any direction, and fortune is not linear. Life is never fixed on a single path, and success is not limited to a predetermined trajectory.

description1: This card is an inversion of priorities, intentional sacrifice. The process of unmaking — releasing, mourning, and dissolving — is an active engagement with the forces of transformation rather than a passive experience. Death reminds us that the only path forward is through adaptation, surrender to change, and the courageous embrace of transition.

Strange strangers, illusions, and shifting perceptions are part of the terrain; staying curious and attentive allows navigation through the vast and often haunting inner landscape.

description2:
The Sun also emphasizes wholeness and integration. 
The act of being oneself, honestly and clearly, generates illumination for both the self and those around them.

description1: This card represents threshold moments, the call to awaken. It is a signal that lasting decisions or weighty choices must be faced. This archetype emphasizes awareness and responsibility. Just as the Egyptian goddess Maat weighed the heart against the feather, Judgment asks us to consider the alignment of our actions, intentions, and values. It is the trumpet that calls for reflection, transformation, and the embracing of potential beyond the past.

name: The World

description1: The manifest world. All of it. The whole, difficult, luminous, heartbreaking sum. Presided over by Saturn, the oldest and heaviest of the planets, whose rings encircle it like a boundary around everything that can be known. Saturn respects the person who shows up anyway, who works within the walls of the possible, who does not demand that reality be other than it is. The World is not given. It is earned — through time, through effort, through the willingness to remain present in the face of everything that life requires.

This decan juxtaposes the advantages and dangers of luxurious excess with the truth of scarcity... In a world of limited material resources, the attainment of luxury for one entails deprivation for others... It is therefore of vital importance in this decan (card) to share, to invest the excess that one acquires in good works - to be a conduit for luxury, not its endpoint.2
description1: This is a very lunar card as the moon rules both the decan and the sign.

Hunger is both the pleasure and the cost of being alive, and every being must eventually confront that cycle.

It reflects harmonious connections, where affection and passion flow without pretense or rigid decorum. Poignant and simple, it is an ideal of how relationships can feel when trust is firmly established.

Moros (diamon of doom) whispers that it is pointless, and that the wheel of incarnation is merely a cruel carnival ride. In argument, Elpis points to beauty, love, and the real possibility of happy endings. The last decan is this a miniature of all incarnation, asking the most important questions and offering the most impassioned answers.2
